# infrawrench_slo (Resource)

A service-level objective: a target over a rolling window, measured from data Infrawrench already records. The SLI is the share of good minutes in the window, from a synthetic probe's success ratio, the share of its checks under a latency threshold, or the share of minutes a resource's metric satisfies a comparison.

The poller computes the error budget and multiwindow burn rates every minute and routes `sloAlerts` through the organization's alert routing rules: a page when 2% of the budget burns in an hour or 5% in six hours, a ticket-level alert when 10% burns in three days. When the budget runs out and `suggest_freeze` is set, the alert suggests a change freeze; nothing is frozen until somebody starts one.

Only the source fields the `sli_kind` uses may be set. Unlike probes, an out-of-range value is rejected rather than clamped.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "infrawrench_probe" "api" {
  name = "API health"
  url  = "https://api.example.com/health"
}

# 99.9% of probe checks succeed over a rolling 30 days: 43 minutes of budget.
resource "infrawrench_slo" "api_availability" {
  name           = "API availability"
  sli_kind       = "probe_availability"
  probe_id       = infrawrench_probe.api.id
  target_percent = 99.9
  window_days    = 30
}

# 99% of checks answer within 300 ms over 28 days.
resource "infrawrench_slo" "api_latency" {
  name                 = "API latency"
  sli_kind             = "probe_latency"
  probe_id             = infrawrench_probe.api.id
  latency_threshold_ms = 300
  target_percent       = 99
  window_days          = 28
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Unique in the organization; 1–120 characters.
- `sli_kind` (String) Where the SLI comes from: one of `probe_availability`, `probe_latency`, `metric_threshold`. `probe_availability` and `probe_latency` need `probe_id`; `probe_latency` also needs `latency_threshold_ms`; `metric_threshold` needs `resource_id`, `metric_key`, `comparator` and `threshold`.
- `target_percent` (Number) The objective as a percentage, 50–99.999. `99.9` over 30 days is 43 minutes of budget.

### Optional

- `alerts_enabled` (Boolean) Route burn-rate and exhaustion alerts. Burn rates are computed either way.
- `comparator` (String) `metric_threshold`: a minute is good when `value <comparator> threshold`. One of `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`.
- `description` (String) Free text shown under the name; 1–500 characters.
- `enabled` (Boolean) A disabled SLO is not evaluated and raises no alerts.
- `latency_threshold_ms` (Number) `probe_latency`: a check is good at or under this many milliseconds, 1–60000.
- `metric_key` (String) `metric_threshold`: the series label as the resource reports it, for example `CPU %`; 1–200 characters.
- `probe_id` (String) `probe_*`: the `infrawrench_probe` to measure. Deleting the probe does not delete the SLO; it goes to `unknown` until it is pointed at another one.
- `resource_id` (String) `metric_threshold`: the Infrawrench resource whose metric is measured. Use `data.infrawrench_resources` to resolve one; it must have reported metrics recently.
- `suggest_freeze` (Boolean) When the budget runs out, the alert and the SLO's page suggest a change freeze.
- `threshold` (Number) `metric_threshold`: the right-hand side of the comparison, in the metric's unit.
- `window_days` (Number) Rolling window in days: `7`, `28` or `30`. Defaults to `30`.

### Read-Only

- `budget_remaining` (Number) Share of the window's error budget left, as a fraction; negative when overspent.
- `budget_remaining_minutes` (Number) `budget_remaining` in minutes; negative when overspent.
- `budget_total_minutes` (Number) The window's whole error budget in minutes of total badness.
- `id` (String) Server-assigned SLO id. Use it with `terraform import`.
- `sli` (Number) Share of good minutes over the window, as a fraction; null with no data.
- `status` (String) The last evaluation, worst first: `exhausted`, `fast_burn`, `slow_burn`, `ok`, or `unknown` (no data in the window, never evaluated, or disabled).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The id is in the URL when you open the SLO in the app, and in the --json
# output of `infrawrench slos`.
terraform import infrawrench_slo.example 3c4d5e6f-7a8b-4c9d-8e0f-1a2b3c4d5e6f
```
